newsitem.title: USA: US Treasury's Summers rejects new tax approach.
newsitem.headline: US Treasury's Summers rejects new tax approach.

text.p: Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said Thursday the Clinton administration rejected the idea that the United States should unilaterally move to a new system for taxing companies that operate across international borders.

In remarks prepared for delivery to a conference on international taxation, Summers said, "The formula apportionment system is not a realistic alternative to the arm's length standard" currently used.
He added it was unlikely other countries would adopt formula apportionment even if the U.S. proposed doing so.

Summers said moving to a new tax system unilaterally "would severely disrupt world business" and would appear contradictory since the United States has worked to strengthen support for the current approach.

Some members of Congress support the formula apportionment system, saying it would capture more revenue from foreign companies operating in the United States by preventing them from manipulating prices they charge each other for goods and services.

"The United States would, in all likelihood, be isolated if we unilaterally adopted formula apportionment," Summers said. "The resulting overlap of incompatible approaches would destroy our network of tax treaties and severely harm the ability of our companies to compete on the world stage."
Given the high degree of cooperation that would be needed to implement a changed tax regime, "the U.S. cannot and should not move forward alone," Summers added.
